feed.title: The Launch Report
feed.subtitle: Rocket launches, reentries and the business of spaceflight, worldwide
feed.rights: The Launch Report is compiled from official agency releases, regulatory filings, orbital tracking data, public posts on X and published reporting. Quotes are reproduced verbatim unless marked as translated or paraphrased. Launch times change often; check with the launch provider before making plans.

entry.title: Thursday, November 12, 2026: Vulcan returns and Starship goes for a double catch on Friday
entry.summary:
Two orbital launches flew worldwide since Monday's issue, and both reached orbit: a Long March 2D from Jiuquan with the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Pathfinder-1 science satellite on Wednesday morning, and a Falcon 9 from Vandenberg with the classified USSF-627 mission late Wednesday night, two days later than planned. That brings 2026 to 262 orbital launch attempts and 255 successes, counting GCAT through Sunday and the two launches since.

Friday is the big day. United Launch Alliance's (ULA) Vulcan flies for the first time in more than nine months with 40 Amazon Leo satellites at 12:54 p.m., and the FAA's airspace plan now carries Starship Flight 15 at 5:45 p.m., with a first attempt to catch both the booster and the ship (FAA). Rocket Lab's 100th Electron follows early Saturday. South Korea's military rocket demonstration is off again after a diver died working on its launch barge, and NASA's twin ESCAPADE probes are now headed for Mars.

entry.title: Monday, November 9, 2026: Five for five, and Starship lines up a double catch
entry.summary:
Five orbital launches flew worldwide since Thursday's issue, and all five reached orbit: a Long March 2C with three Yaogan-51 satellites, Galactic Energy's Ceres-2 on its first successful flight, SpaceX's USSF-432 from Vandenberg, a Soyuz with the Glonass navigation satellite Kosmos 2621, and a Long March 12 with SatNet internet satellites. That brings 2026 to 260 orbital launch attempts and 253 successes, according to GCAT.

Friday, November 13, is shaping up as the busiest day ahead: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan returns with 40 Amazon Leo satellites, and SpaceX says Starship Flight 15 is "targeting to launch as early as Friday, November 13, pending regulatory approval," with an attempt to catch both stages (SpaceX). On the station, Thursday's spacewalk installed the last of eight roll-out solar arrays, and Varda's W-8 capsule came home.

entry.title: Thursday, November 5, 2026: Electron's 99th and a Spacesail cluster open November
entry.summary:
Two orbital launches flew worldwide since Monday's issue, both successful. Rocket Lab's Electron lofted a Japanese radar satellite on its 99th flight Monday morning from Mahia, and China's Kinetica 2 put 18 Spacesail communications satellites into polar orbit Monday evening from Jiuquan. That brings 2026 to 255 orbital launch attempts, 248 of them successful, according to GCAT plus Monday's flights from Launch Library 2.

USSF-432 has slipped again, to Friday night in the FAA plan, and Starlink 15-21 is off the near-term board. NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory reentered Wednesday over Indonesia after nearly 22 years, and Canadian and NASA astronauts were due outside the International Space Station this morning to install the final roll-out solar array.

entry.title: Monday, November 2, 2026: India's NVS-03 and the 700th Falcon 9 close out October
entry.summary:
Two orbital launches flew worldwide since Thursday's issue. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) put the NVS-03 navigation satellite into orbit on a Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) Friday afternoon, and SpaceX launched Starlink 15-18 from Vandenberg just after midnight Saturday, the 700th Falcon 9 flight. That brings 2026 to 253 orbital launch attempts, 246 of them successful, according to GCAT, and October ended with every launch a success.

Nine more launches have dates in the coming week, starting with Rocket Lab's 99th Electron at 11:41 a.m. Monday. The U.S. Space Force mission USSF-432 has moved to Tuesday night in Launch Library 2. On the International Space Station, Thursday's spacewalk installed a new roll-out solar array, and the final power-upgrade spacewalk is set for November 5.

entry.title: Thursday, October 29, 2026: One launch since Monday; Vulcan returns November 13
entry.summary:
The only orbital launch worldwide since Monday's issue was SpaceX's Starlink 15-16, which left Vandenberg at 3:25 a.m. EDT Tuesday. That brings 2026 to 251 orbital launch attempts, 244 of them successful, according to GCAT. ISRO's GSLV with the NVS-03 navigation satellite is set for 2:21 p.m. Friday, and Starlink 15-18 follows from Vandenberg late Friday night.

United Launch Alliance says Vulcan will return to flight on Friday, November 13, carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites, after a nine-month grounding over solid rocket booster nozzle problems. On the International Space Station, NASA's Anil Menon and the Canadian Space Agency's Joshua Kutryk began a spacewalk at 8:13 a.m. Thursday to install a new solar array.

entry.title: Monday, October 26, 2026: Five launches, five successes since Thursday
entry.summary:
Rocket Lab's Electron put three HawkEye 360 satellites in orbit early Friday, China flew three Long March rockets from Taiyuan, Jiuquan and Wenchang between Friday morning and Saturday night, and Starlink 15-15 finally left Vandenberg on Friday evening after three earlier scrubs. That brings 2026 to 250 orbital launch attempts, 243 of them successful, according to GCAT.

Two Vandenberg Starlinks have moved a day later, India's GSLV now has a firm date of Friday, and United Launch Alliance's Vulcan with Amazon Leo LV-01 has slipped from late October into November. In Texas, Starship's Booster 22 completed a full-duration static fire on Sunday ahead of Flight 15.

entry.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026: MMX is on its way to Mars; three launches, three successes since Monday
entry.summary:
Japan's H3 sent the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe toward Mars at 3:41 p.m. EDT Monday, a Falcon 9 flew the Bandwagon-5 rideshare from Florida on Tuesday morning, and Galactic Energy launched a Ceres-1S from the sea off eastern China that night. That brings 2026 to 246 orbital launch attempts, 239 of them successful, counting GCAT through October 15 and Launch Library 2 since.

Two launches stood down. Thunderstorms scrubbed Starlink 15-15 at Vandenberg on Wednesday, a day after a technical issue stopped it, and Rocket Lab postponed an Electron for HawkEye 360 to review "out-of-family telemetry data." Both have new dates this week, as do three Long March rockets.

entry.title: Monday, October 19, 2026: One launch since Thursday; H3 sends MMX toward Mars this afternoon
entry.summary:
The only orbital launch anywhere since Thursday's issue was the classified USSF-481 mission, which a Falcon 9 lifted from Vandenberg at 8:01 p.m. EDT Thursday. That brings 2026 to 243 orbital launch attempts, 236 of them successful, according to GCAT. Bandwagon-5, set for this morning, slipped to Tuesday because of weather in the booster recovery zone, SpaceX posted.

Japan's H3 is due to launch the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe at 3:41:03 p.m. EDT today, and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) has extended its reserve period to November 9. Eight more orbital launches are dated through Saturday: four Chinese, three by SpaceX and one by Rocket Lab. Rocket Lab pushed the first Neutron flight to 2027.

entry.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026: Three launches since Monday, Dragon arrives today, and a Space Force flight tonight
entry.summary:
SpaceX launched twice in ten hours, sending 27 Starlink satellites up from California on Monday night and NASA's CRS-35 cargo Dragon toward the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday morning. On Wednesday, China's LandSpace put ten satellites in orbit on a methane-fueled Zhuque-2E, eight of them for an orbital computing constellation. That brings 2026 to 242 orbital launch attempts, according to GCAT.

Dragon is due to dock at about 11 a.m. EDT today, and a Falcon 9 launches the classified USSF-481 mission from Vandenberg at 7:44 p.m. EDT. Japan's H3 carries the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe on Monday. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) opened an environmental review of up to 456 Starship launches a year from Starbase, Texas, and ISRO's NVS-03 window opens today with no launch date announced.

entry.title: Monday, October 12, 2026: The SDA batch finally flies, China adds 27th SatNet group, and three old stages come home
entry.summary:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 carried 21 Space Development Agency (SDA) satellites to orbit from California at 3:39 a.m. EDT Saturday, five days after an abort at T-minus 58 seconds. Eleven hours earlier, at 3:27 p.m. EDT Friday, a Long March 12 lifted off from Hainan with the 27th group of China's SatNet low-orbit internet satellites. Those were the world's only two orbital launches since Thursday, according to Launch Library 2, bringing 2026 to 239 attempts.

All three rocket stages predicted to reenter on Saturday, including a Delta 2 stage launched in 1990, did so, according to CelesTrak. This week brings a Starlink launch Monday night, NASA's CRS-35 cargo flight to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday and a U.S. Space Force mission on Thursday, with Japan's H3 and its Mars-moon probe a week out. Elon Musk said Starship's next flight is four to six weeks away and will try to catch the ship itself.

entry.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026: Nuri goes four for four, Crew-12 comes home, and a Mars-moon mission heads for the pad
entry.summary:
South Korea's Nuri rocket put 14 satellites in orbit on Wednesday, its fourth success in a row. It was the only orbital launch anywhere in the world between Monday and Thursday morning, according to Launch Library 2. A SpaceX Falcon 9 carrying 21 Space Development Agency (SDA) satellites aborted at T-minus one minute on Monday and is now set for 3:29 a.m. EDT Saturday. On Thursday, the Crew-12 astronauts splashed down off Los Angeles after 237 days on the International Space Station (ISS).

The next two weeks are busier: a Long March 12 from Hainan on Friday, three more Falcon 9 launches, and NASA's 35th Commercial Resupply Services cargo flight (CRS-35) on Tuesday. Then, on October 19, Japan's H3 rocket launches the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe, which is designed to return samples from the Martian moon Phobos. Three old rocket stages are predicted to fall back to Earth on Saturday. In Washington, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has proposed loosening five launch-safety rules.
